an advanced interactive image gallery rendered entirely on an html5 canvas. the script maps a collection of unsplash images onto the surface of a virtual 3d sphere, calculating scale and opacity based on their normalized distance from the center. users can rotate the sphere via mouse or touch drag. hovering over an image highlights it with a tracking focus box, and clicking expands the image with a procedural slicing animation, accompanied by random digital glitch effects.

this cinematic travel presentation combines scroll-driven vector mapping and nested photographic galleries. built with gsap scrolltrigger and the intersection observer api, scrolling initiates a staged intro: the title fades, a detailed svg map draws its borders, and a specific province highlights. concurrently, a three-column image grid slides up, transitioning smoothly from greyscale to full color.

an interactive scroll-driven showcase featuring godzilla walking across a detailed scenic skyline. scrolling horizontally advances the sprite along an svg vector path using gsap motionpath and scrolltrigger, adjusting container offsets to dynamically re-center the camera viewpoint. features vintage film grain dust loops, click-to-destroy targets, and explosive debris particles.

an advanced scroll-driven webgl experience powered by three.js and gsap. a fixed background canvas uses instancedmesh to render nearly 50,000 distinct 3d cube particles, colored dynamically by extracting color values from an image mapped onto a hidden canvas. as the user scrolls down the page, the camera’s z-axis position transitions, causing the scattered cubes to seamlessly converge into a photographic portrait.

this is a smooth parallax image scroll gallery. it translates vertical scroll progression into independent y-axis movement for masked images. its function is to create a sense of depth and momentum, elevating standard vertical feeds into immersive visual narratives.

this is a staggered text scroll reveal. it parses structural typography into independent animated lines. its function is to pace the reader’s attention, transforming static paragraphs into dynamic narrative elements triggered by viewport intersection.

this is a twisted wave glsl image gallery. it’s a high-performance, full-screen webgl experience that uses custom shaders to create sophisticated visual effects. its function is to transform a standard image carousel into a cinematic journey with two distinct interactions: a localized sine-wave distortion on mouse hover and a global radial blur that intensifies with the speed of the scroll.

this snippet showcases a gsap scrolltrigger list expansion effect. it mimics the native ios “notification center” or “wallet” card stack behavior. its function is to condense a long list of items into a compact, layered visual stack, and then fluidly expand them into full, scrollable cards as the user scrolls down the container, creating a highly tactile mobile ui experience.

this is a cinematic zoom blur image gallery. it utilizes custom glsl fragment shaders and three.js to create a high-fidelity transition between image textures. its function is to provide an immersive navigational layer for visual portfolios, where spatial depth and radial blur replace standard linear crossfades.

this is a scroll-driven jigsaw puzzle assembler. it utilizes svg patterns and css variables to deconstruct a single image into interactive, interlocking pieces. its function is to provide a cinematic content reveal where scrolling physically assembles the visual asset from a scattered state into a coherent whole.

this is a lenis smooth scroll cinematic experience. it transforms a standard single-page portfolio or narrative website into an immersive, high-end digital journey. its primary function is to replace jarring browser scrolling with the fluid, physics-based motion of lenis, while using gsap’s scrolltrigger plugin to orchestrate a complex sequence of cinematic animations, including a “film roll” header, an expanding video player, and a dramatic footer reveal.

this is a shattering image gallery transition. it utilizes the webgl api via three.js to deconstruct 2d images into a matrix of 3d particles. its function is to replace standard fade or slide slideshows with a highly cinematic, physics-based explosion effect, transitioning between photographs by blowing the current image apart to reveal the next one underneath.

experience a classic “pinned” horizontal scroll effect, where a vertical scroll action is converted into horizontal movement. gsap’s pin: true property freezes the section in place, while a tween animates the x property of the inner container, creating a cinematic, side-scrolling gallery.

this demo uses a single scroll event listener to calculate the individual progress of each list item as it enters the viewport. the progress value is then passed to a css custom property, which drives a staggered transform: scale() and opacity animation for a fluid, app-like reveal effect.

this infinitely scrolling image grid employs an intersectionobserver with baton-passing observation to dynamically load content from the pixabay api, creating cards through dom manipulation as the user scrolls. javascript manages the paginated requests while css grid provides responsive layout adaptation, with custom properties enabling seamless dark/light theme switching and clip-path animations.

a smooth vertical timeline featuring scroll-triggered element animation, implemented using efficient pure javascript dom visibility tracking to enhance performance and content engagement.

an elegant text reveal effect that uses the intersection observer api for lazy-loading animation upon entering the viewport and relies on gsap to perform a smooth “wipe” using a scale transformation.
Dinosaur Park Scroll Snap Reveal Demo
impressive scroll-triggered element reveal implemented using the native intersection observer api and styling based on css custom properties for cascading animations.
a demo of the scroll zoom effect via dynamic element visibility calculation and utilizing the intersection observer api for performance enhancement.
Layout Explorations with GSAP, Flip, Lenis and ScrollTrigger N°2

an advanced gallery ux pattern where view switching (list/grid) uses gsap flip for calculating and executing complex transitions, and the hover preview effect is controlled by precise mouse events with debounce logic.
an interactive demo showcasing slide transitions via destructive digital effects. it uses webgl shaders to create realistic vhs distortion, static, and pixelation.

technically, this is an example of using gsap for “in” and “out” element animations based on scroll position. the code effectively uses callback functions like onenter, onenterback, and onleave to manage element states, making them visible only when needed.
Wave and RGB Image Distortion with Shaders

see how vertex and fragment shaders in three.js are used to create a “living image” effect that reacts to scrolling. the technical focus is on the deformation (uoffset) and rgb shift (urgbshift) controlled via gsap.
Infinite Horizontal Scroll with Progress Tracking
a fullscreen horizontal scroll with unique infinite loop logic based on dynamic content cloning, complemented by a progress indicator.

just an avatar button. press it and the menu springs out of the avatar: a name line, profile, settings and help, and a red log out rise in one after another. press again, hit esc or click outside and it folds back into the avatar.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a small cookie consent card with a golden chocolate-chip cookie perched on top that wobbles now and then. press allow and a bite comes out of the cookie as crumbs tumble down; a beat later the card shrinks into a “thanks” pill with the bitten cookie as its icon and floats away. press essential only and the cookie shrinks to crumb size while the card quietly tucks away.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a compact cookie settings sheet. essential stays on with a little lock, while the analytics, marketing and functional switches stretch their squishy thumbs as you press. each switch you turn on presses a chocolate chip into the cookie up top, and turning it off pops it back out. saving makes the cookie hop.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

an agreement sheet with just agree to all and three terms. checking agree to all draws the checks down the list one after another, and the moment both required items are on, the agree and continue button fills from left to right and wakes up. pick only some and agree to all shows a half-filled mark.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)
a phone-width header bar. press the hamburger and its two bars become an x while the bar grows downward, dropping the menu links in turn and finishing with a get started button.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a single product button with a dropdown of four icon items. rest the pointer on it and the menu springs open from the button as the chevron flips; move across the items and a soft highlight glides along with you.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a pill with one announcement — “new feature · learn more →”. three notices roll upward every few seconds and pause under the pointer. press × and the pill folds smoothly into a single sparkle button; press that button to open it again.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a single breadcrumb trail from home to the current page. the middle steps sit folded behind …; press it and they spring open sideways. press a step and the trail after it folds away as that step becomes the current page.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a three-part segmented tab with a small panel underneath. pick a tab and the thumb stretches from its leading edge, then its trailing edge catches up like jelly, while the panel content glides in from the direction you moved.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)
an app sidebar with icons and labels. pick an item and the highlight springs over to it; press the round button on the edge and the width bounces down to an icon-only rail as the labels melt away.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)
a calm footer with a wordmark, three short link groups, social icons and a copyright line. hover a link and an underline draws in from the left; social icons bounce up and take on their brand colors.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a hero text block: a new-release badge, a two-line headline, one subline and two buttons. the headline rises word by word from below and settles, with the last word glowing in a gradient. hover the buttons and their arrows push forward.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

four feature tiles with an icon, a name and one line each. hover or focus a tile and it lifts slightly while its icon plays its own little motion: two cursors meet, a sparkle spins, a bolt zaps and a lock clicks open and shut.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)
a single row of fictional customer wordmarks drifts slowly, fading out at both ends. hover and the flow glides to a stop while only the logo under the pointer sharpens.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

one testimonial card with two more peeking from behind. every few seconds the top card tilts and flies off to the side while the next one springs forward, its stars filling in one by one. you can drag the card away yourself, too.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)
a monthly / yearly toggle above a single pro plan card. pick yearly and the thumb slides over, the price digits roll like an odometer, and a “2 months free” badge springs in.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)
a four-question accordion. press a question and its answer unfolds smoothly while the plus sign’s vertical stroke turns flat into a minus. only one stays open at a time.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a call-to-action card with one bold line and a single button on a gradient. a soft glow follows the pointer across the card, and a streak of light sweeps the button every few seconds. press it and it squishes, then springs back.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)
a stats card with three big numbers split by hairlines. when it comes into view each digit rolls like an odometer and settles on its number; hover a number and it rolls around once more.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

an email field with a subscribe button. a mistyped address makes the field give a little shake, and subscribing shrinks the button into a circle with a check while a tiny envelope with a heart seal flies off.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a contact form with name, email and message fields and a send button. send it and the form folds down to envelope size, the flap closes, a heart seal stamps on and the envelope flies away, leaving “sent” in its place.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

type into a search field with a ⌘k hint and four suggestions pop open below, the matching letters in bold. press ↑↓ and the selection bar springs from row to row; press enter and the list folds away as the field fills in.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)
press the assignee button and a list of four people springs open. type a name and it filters instantly; pick someone and the check mark pops over to them while the button takes on the new assignee.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)
a single-month calendar. tap a day and the selection circle springs over to it; change months and the calendar slides sideways. today is marked with a dot, and past days can’t be picked.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a drop zone for files. drag one over and the border comes alive; let go and a document drops in from above and settles. a ring around it fills as it uploads, and when it’s full a green check pops out.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

the three basic selection controls, tuned to feel good. the checkbox bounces as its check draws in, the radio dot springs over to the other option, and the switch thumb stretches while you press it before gliding across.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)
a single email field walks through its states. tap it and the border glows softly; pause with a malformed address and it shakes its head as a red hint slides down; fix it and a green check pops out.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

press save and a toast springs up from below, a check draws itself and a thin time bar runs down. press again and toasts stack like a deck (up to three); hover and they fan out while the timers pause. flick one sideways or press × to dismiss, and undo turns the toast into “undone”.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)
a dialog that asks once more before a delete you can’t undo. press delete and the trash can’s lid flips open, a document drops in, the lid snaps shut, and the dialog gently goes away.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)
a three-button toolbar. rest on a button and a tooltip with an arrow pops out of it, showing the name and shortcut; slide to the next button and it glides along with no second wait.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

press publish and the button squishes, its label fades as it shrinks into a circle and starts to spin. when it’s done, a check draws itself inside a mint circle, then the button stretches back to full width and the label returns.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

while an article card loads, bones in the exact place and size of the real content shimmer to hold the space; when it arrives, the image, title and author fade in over them one after another. the button below loads it again.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)
the first screen of an empty workspace. an empty folder bobs gently in the air; press “create first project” and a document drops into the folder, the folder bounces and sparkles burst.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)
a shop product card. pick a color chip and the tumbler in the photo shifts color with a little bounce; the heart pops as it fills. press add and the button turns into a check before coming back.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)
press add and the product photo arcs through the air into the cart, the cart gives a little wiggle, and its badge bounces up by one.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)
radio cards for credit or debit card, kakao pay, naver pay and toss pay, each with its brand mark. choose one and the selection outline springs over to it while the dot inside the circle pops up.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)
steps running cart → shipping → payment → done. moving on fills the line between steps, a check pops onto each finished step, and the current step breathes with a soft ring.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a coupon ticket and a code field. enter the code and apply it: an “applied” stamp thumps onto the ticket, the original price is struck through, and the number rolls down to the discounted price. a wrong code makes the field shake its head.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a summary with just the average and the distribution. as it comes into view, 4.6 counts up from zero, the stars fill from the left in half-star steps and five bars fill in one after another. hover a bar and only that row lights up while its percentage turns into a review count.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a single dark mode switch with a sky painted inside. press it and the sun rolls across into a cratered moon, the blue daytime sky deepens to navy, the clouds sink away and stars drop in to twinkle. its colors live inside the switch and never depend on the page theme.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a globe button and a list of five languages. press it and the list springs out of the button, each language written in its own script. pick one and the globe turns as its meridians roll past, while the button label changes to the new language name and smoothly resizes.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

just the page-number bar. the pill around the current page springs over to the next number, and when the window shifts, ellipses and numbers roll up or down into each other. there are always seven slots so the bar never changes width, and the previous and next buttons dim at the ends.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

two buttons floating in the bottom-right corner. the upper back to top button carries a ring filled as far as you have read; press it and the arrow shoots up as the ring unwinds, then it tucks away for a moment. the lower chat bubble swells into a compact support panel right where it sits, and shrinks back into a round button when closed.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

type @ in a comment box and a member list pops open right under that character, then filters as you keep typing. pick with ↑↓ and press enter: the name drops in as a violet mention chip with a little bounce. press backspace right after a chip and the whole chip goes at once.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

the prompt box of an ai app. as you write, the box grows upward line by line and the send button wakes up. send and your text flies up, the arrow morphs into a stop square and a thin light runs around the border; when the answer is done it turns back into an arrow. tap the model pill and the model name rolls over.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

the “thinking…” line an ai shows before it answers. a soft light sweeps across the words while the star beside them slowly turns and breathes. tap it to expand and the thoughts stream in one line at a time; when it’s done it folds itself away and settles into a calm “thought for 4s”. you can still tap it afterwards to read the thoughts again.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

shows the order an ai agent works in as a vertical list. read files → make a plan → edit code → run tests each spin in turn and pop into a check, the line joining the steps fills downward and a result lands on the right. when everything is done the bottom row turns into a “done” summary, and ↻ runs it again.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

the approval card an ai agent shows before it runs a terminal command. press allow and the card shrinks into a one-line pill that spins, then lands on a “12 tests passed” check; press deny and a line strikes through the command. turn on always allow before allowing and the pill keeps a small badge. a moment later the next request unfolds again.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

pause while writing and the rest of the sentence fades in after the caret in grey, with a tiny tab keycap at the end. press tab and ink spreads from the left as the grey text fills in solid and becomes yours; press esc and it blurs away. keep typing the same letters and the grey text shrinks to match.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

press the mic button and it stretches into a pill with a waveform that sways with your voice and a recording timer beside a blinking red dot. press stop and the waveform flattens into a line as the pill shrinks into a chip of the transcribed sentence, its words floating up one by one. the mic at the end of the chip lets you speak again.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

the glowing orb of a voice assistant. each tap changes its state: waiting, it breathes slowly; listening, ripples spread outward; thinking, the light inside swirls fast and the orb draws in a little; speaking, it pulses like syllables. the motion carries on smoothly from one state to the next.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a single black pill holds live activities. tap it and it springs open with a wobble; swipe it sideways and it reshapes into a timer, then music, then an incoming call. the timer really counts down, the equalizer dances while music plays (with play and skip), and the call can be answered or declined. the pill stays black whatever the page theme.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

press the floating + button and a soft blob stretches like a droplet, then splits off into four action buttons (photo, camera, voice memo, file) as the + turns into an ×. close it or pick an action and the buttons get sucked back in stickily and merge into one again.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a boarding pass from incheon to jeju. hover and the card tilts as if held in your hand, the route and the little plane drift on their own layers, and a holographic sheen slides across. drag the seat stub to the right of the perforation and it tears from the top; pull far enough and it snaps free, wobbling on a spring as it settles beside the card. let go too early and it springs back into place.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a “slide to pay” track. a soft light sweeps across the label; drag the round thumb and the path behind it fills in while the label fades. reach the end and the track squishes down into a mint “paid” pill as a check draws itself. let go halfway and the thumb springs back, squashing gently against the wall. with a keyboard, press enter or use the arrow keys.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a dial modeled on the volume knob of an audio component. turn the knurled knob and it clicks from tick to tick as if each one catches, lighting the ticks it passes while the speaker icon’s waves and the number below update. let go and it springs a hair past the nearest tick before settling. arrow keys turn it one step at a time.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

an exposure compensation ruler from a camera app. the center needle stays put while you drag the ruler sideways; the value changes every third of a stop and the landscape photo above darkens or brightens to match. flick it and it coasts on momentum before springing onto the nearest tick, and pushing past the ends feels like a rubber band. tap a tick to jump there, or double-tap to return to zero.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a mustard pendant lamp hanging from the ceiling with a pull cord dangling beneath it. pull the wooden bead down and let go: the cord springs back up and swings, and the shade sways along with it. in that moment the bulb flickers once or twice, then pours warm light downward; pull again and the light fades slowly away. the illustration’s colors stay the same in either theme.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a focus mode card sits among four floating notification chips. switch it on and the chips blur and fall back one by one, while a ring fills around the moon icon and a 25:00 timer quietly starts counting down. the ring breathes with a soft glow; switch it off and time stops as the chips bounce back in turn.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a one-line bio field that takes up to 40 characters. as you type, a small ring in the corner fills; with 8 left it grows and turns amber to show how many remain. go past 40 and the ring turns red, the card gives a little head-shake, the overflow gets a red highlighter and save locks. delete a few and everything calms down again.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a pad for signing with a finger or a pen. slow strokes come out bold and quick ones thin, so the line carries weight like a real pen. press done and the signature fades for a beat, then lands with a thump as a red-ink stamp, with “signed” and the date set into its border. clear lets you start over at any time.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a little jeju travel journal with photos pasted in. hover the right page and its corner lifts; press it or drag it left and the paper curls as it turns. while it turns, the curved paper picks up shading and casts a shadow on the page below; it follows your drag and, when you let go, settles softly onto the nearer side. press the left page to go back.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

press a trash button in the file list and that row slides aside and disappears while the rows below glide up. at the same moment an “undo” pill springs up at the bottom, its ring shrinking over five seconds as a number counts down. press it and the row bounces back into place; leave it and the pill drops away as the delete becomes final. hovering the pill pauses the timer.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a “search docs” button with ⌘ and k keycaps on its right. press ⌘k or click it and the two keycaps sink one after the other and spring back, a ripple spreads from the keys and the button squishes and bounces. hold ⌘ alone and the k keycap breathes, asking to be pressed. off a mac it shows ctrl instead of ⌘.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a storage bar split into photos, apps, documents, other and free space. when it scrolls into view the segments grow in one after another while the “96.4 gb of 128 gb used” figure counts up. hover a segment or a legend item and that segment swells while the rest fade back, and the usage line rolls over to show its name, size and share.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a team invite card. type an email and press enter (or a comma) and the address pops out as a chip with a round initial avatar; below it you choose can edit or can view. press send invites and the chips shrink down to their avatars, then arc one after another into the member avatar stack up top, each landing with a check badge.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a frosted-glass mini player lit from behind by the sunset colors of its album art. press play and the triangle splits into two bars, the album art springs up from its resting size and the glow behind it brightens and breathes. grab the progress bar and it thickens while the time follows along.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a “new” pill button stretches as one continuous shape into a menu panel. width, height and corners swell together with a little overshoot, the + turns into ×, and document, folder, upload and template rise in one after another. pick one and the panel shrinks back into the pill, a check spins in for the + and the pill briefly reshapes around “folder created” before settling.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

press listen and the paragraph lights up word by word at reading pace, each word filling from the left while a violet underline follows up to where it has read. the triangle splits into a pause icon, and pressing again picks up right where it stopped. click any word to jump there.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a compact emoji picker that sits under a chat bubble, with search, a row of recent emoji and smileys, gestures, hearts, food and activity tabs. the emoji under the pointer plumps up; pick one and it arcs up and pops onto the corner of the bubble as a reaction, and slips into the front of the recent row too.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a share card that hands over a link as a qr code. the code isn’t a picture: the address is really encoded and drawn as svg, so a phone camera opens it. when it scrolls into view the corner brackets close in and a beam of light sweeps down across it. press copy link and the button turns mint, reading copied as a check draws in.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

an hsv color picker with a saturation–value square, a hue bar, a hex field and four swatches. the handles plump up when pressed, and when you click elsewhere or change the color from a swatch or the hex field they glide to the new spot with a springy overshoot. the preview chip on the left switches its text between white and black, whichever reads better on the chosen color. arrow keys work too.
open source, free incl. commercial (author post)

a six-digit pin keypad like the ones in banking apps. the digits come shuffled each time, and every press pops a dot full. a wrong pin turns the dots red, shakes them side to side, clears them and reshuffles the keys. the right one draws the six dots together into a single mint circle that becomes a check.
